{{recipe}} 

Chipotles add a Southwestern smoky heat to otherwise normal fish n' chips.

== Ingredients ==

=== Chipotle vinegar ===
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Malt vinegar|malt vinegar]]
*2-3 canned [[Cookbook:Chipotle Pepper|chipotle chiles]] in adobo, pureed until smooth
*Pinch of salt

=== Fish ===
* 1 bottle (12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) very cold [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Cornmeal|cornmeal]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] Old Bay seasoning
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* 1 tbsp salt
* 3–4 canned [[Cookbook:Chipotle Pepper|chipotle chiles]] in adobo, pureed until smooth
* 1–2 tbsp adobo sauce
* [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|Cornstarch]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tilapia|tilapia]] fillets, cut into 1-[[Cookbook:Ounce|ounce]] strips
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]] for [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep frying]]

=== Serving ===
*1 recipe [[Cookbook:Fast Food French Fries|French fries]], instead of black pepper use chipotle powder

== Procedure ==
#Make the chipotle vinegar by [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisking]] all ingredients in a dipping bowl. Keep at room temperature until needed.
#Combine beer, cornmeal, old bay, worcestershire sauce, salt, chipotles, and adobo to make a [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]].
#[[Cookbook:Dredging|Dredge]] fish pieces in cornstarch, and then dip in the batter.
#[[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] coated fish pieces two at a time in the oil at 350°F. They should take 3 minutes to become golden and crisp on the outside.
#Drain fish pieces on a cooling rack suspended above a baking pan. If inside is undercooked, finish in a 350°F [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]].
#Serve with French fries and the chipotle vinegar.
